lessons.title: Welcome aboard, cadet

modules.title: Your mission briefing
modules.body:
Good morning, cadet. 🚀

In three weeks our crew leaves for **Mars**, the red planet. Before then you'll train: how far it is, what to pack, how to breathe and drink when there's no air or rain, and how to build a base.

Every card is one step of your training. Some cards only appear when you need them, so your board won't look exactly like your friend's.

Ready? Pick your crew job next.

attachments.name: Mars, with the canyon Valles Marineris across the middle

modules.title: Pick your crew job
modules.body: Every crew needs all four jobs. Up to three cadets per job, so pick fast!

questions.text: Which job do you want on the crew?

modules.title: How far is Mars?
modules.body: Mars is our neighbour, but neighbours in space are a long way apart.

questions.text: How long does the trip to Mars take?
questions.explain: With today's rockets it takes about 7 months, when Earth and Mars are on the same side of the Sun.

modules.title: Space is BIG
modules.body:
Not quite! The Moon is 3 days away, but Mars is about **150 times further**.

If you drove a car to Mars at motorway speed without stopping, you'd arrive in about **100 years**. A rocket is much faster, but the trip still takes about **7 months**.

Pack some good books. 📚

lessons.goal: Know where we're going, how far it is, and which job you'll do on the crew.

lessons.title: Pack the rocket

modules.title: What goes on board?
modules.body: Every kilogram costs fuel, so only take what you need.

questions.explain: The bicycle stays home: there are no roads on Mars (yet).

questions.text: Put the launch steps in order.
Which gas do your lungs need? (one word)
Which planet is closest to the Sun?

options: Its dust has rust in it
questions.explain: Mars dust is full of iron oxide: rust!

questions.text: How many moons does Mars have?
questions.explain: Two small ones, Phobos and Deimos. Phobos is only about 22 km across.

modules.title: Refuel: planet facts
modules.body:
Your tank's a bit low, cadet. Top up with these:

- **Mercury** is the closest planet to the Sun. Earth is third, Mars is fourth.
- Mars is red because its dust has **rust** (iron oxide) in it.
- Mars has **two** small moons: Phobos and Deimos.

Then you're cleared for the next lesson.

attachments.name: Phobos, the bigger of Mars's two moons

modules.title: Bonus: the tallest volcano
modules.body: Full tank! 🌋 Here's a reward fact: Mars has **Olympus Mons**, the tallest volcano in the solar system. It's about **22 km** high, nearly three times taller than Mount Everest, and as wide as France.

lessons.goal: Choose what the crew needs, and pass the fuel check.

lessons.title: Build the base

modules.title: Three things to stay alive
modules.body:
On Earth, air, water and food are easy. On Mars:

- The **air** is thin and mostly carbon dioxide. We can't breathe it.
- The **water** is frozen as ice, under the ground and at the poles.
- **Food** has to be grown indoors, under lights, in a greenhouse.

Pass the base inspection, then design your greenhouse.

attachments.name: Jezero crater, seen by the Perseverance rover

questions.text: What is the air on Mars mostly made of?
Can you breathe outside on Mars?
Where is the water on Mars?
How could the crew get drinking water?
options: Dig up ice, melt it and clean it

modules.title: Fix-it list
modules.body:
The inspector found a few problems. 🔧

- The air outside is mostly **carbon dioxide**: always wear your suit.
- There's no rain on Mars. Water comes from **ice**, which we dig up, melt and clean.

Read the first card again, then carry on to the greenhouse.

attachments.name: The ice cap at Mars's north pole

modules.title: Design a Mars greenhouse
modules.body:
Draw your greenhouse (on paper or with **Draw**), then add a photo or your drawing here.

Label:
1. Where the light comes from
2. Where the water comes from
3. Three plants you'd grow, and why

Done when: A labelled drawing with light, water and three plants.

attachments.name: Lettuce grown on the International Space Station

modules.title: What would you miss from Earth?
modules.body: Seven months there, seven months back. What would you miss most? Post one thing, then reply to a classmate.

lessons.goal: Work out how the crew gets air and water, then design a greenhouse for food.

lessons.title: Elective: Rover driving school

modules.title: Meet the rover
modules.body: A rover is a car for Mars, driven from Earth. Radio signals take **up to 20 minutes** to get there, so every turn arrives late. Drivers plan each move carefully, and the rover checks for rocks by itself.

attachments.name: The Curiosity rover takes a selfie

questions.text: Your rover sees a big rock 2 metres ahead. Your command takes 20 minutes to arrive. What should the rover do?
options: Stop and steer around it by itself

lessons.goal: Drive a rover safely across Mars.

lessons.title: Elective: Space kitchen

modules.title: Why crumbs are a problem
modules.body: In a spaceship, crumbs don't fall. They float into eyes, noses and machines! That's why astronauts eat tortillas instead of bread.

attachments.name: Astronaut Peggy Whitson with a “space cheeseburger”

modules.title: Invent a space snack
modules.body: Invent a snack for the trip. Give it a name, say what's in it, and how it stays crumb-free. A drawing or a recording is welcome.

lessons.goal: Invent a snack astronauts can eat without crumbs.

m-o57ayfd.output:
My greenhouse is a dome made of thick clear plastic, half buried so it stays warm.
1. Light: sunlight through the dome, plus LED lamps for dust storms.
2. Water: ice from under the base, melted and cleaned in the tank by the door.
3. Plants: potatoes (lots of food, grow in poor soil), lettuce (fast), and strawberries (for morale!).

review.text: Brilliant, Ava. Half-burying it is exactly what real designs do. Strawberries for morale: approved. 🍓

m-o57ayfd.output: A long glass tunnel with shelves of tomatoes, beans and basil, and big windows for sunlight.

review.text: Lovely plants, Mia! Where does the water come from? Add it to your drawing and hand it in again.

m-o57ayfd.output:
Greenhouse made of ice blocks (ice lets light through and keeps the cold out).
1. Light: the sun shining through the ice.
2. Water: we melt a little of the wall when we need it!
3. Plants: wheat for bread, peas, and sunflowers.
